newsitem.title: USA: U.S. brass mill sales rise in January through July.
newsitem.headline: U.S. brass mill sales rise in January through July.

text.p: Sales of brass mill products in the U.S. rose to 694,300 short tons of copper content in the first seven months of the year compared to 672,600 tons in the same period in 1995, the American Bureau of Metal Statistics reported.
Sales in July fell to 87,400 tons from 97,800 tons in June, and 67,500 tons in July 1995.
Shipments totaled 676,400 tons in the first seven months of the year, up from 665,700 tons in the same period last year.
Shipments in July fell to 85,000 tons from 92,600 tons in June, and 71,100 tons in July 1995.
Inventories of refinery shapes, material in process, and scrap rose to 151,400 tons of copper content by the end of July, up from 149,100 tons at the end of June, and 144,400 tons in July 1995.

Brass scrap consumption fell to 42,100 tons of contained copper in July from 54,400 tons in June. The ABMS said 364,800 tons of copper in brass scrap was consumed in January through July, up from 329,300 tons in the same period last year.
